_readme: The hand-written numbers behind every merchant's market (2026-10-24). tools/gen_markets.js turns this plus the shop data (web/mygame/trade-data.generated.js) into web/mygame/market-data.generated.js; edit THIS file, not the output.

WHAT IT KEEPS THE SAME: at its usual stock a merchant asks exactly the retail price it asks today, and pays today's price (buyPct is worked out from the price it pays now), so nothing changes until stock or purse are pushed. What changes is what happens when they are.
Prices are whole copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper).
purse:     the coin a merchant can pay out (and the target it drifts back to). A stall is a few silver, a shop tens of silver, a city shop tens of gold, a jeweler hundreds.
regen:     the share of the gap to target that stock and purse close each day (0.1 = a tenth).

depthMult: how much more or less than the standard a merchant holds of everything (a city shop deep, a stall shallow). 'depth' is the target stock: how much the merchant wants to hold. A small target moves the price a lot per unit.

tile / commodities: an open market (a village lane, a town's trading ground) on a map tile, dealing in every tagged commodity (see 'commodity' below and tools/gen_markets.js); its goods need no listing here.
buyShare: a market (a village) that pays a set share of the base price for everything it takes, instead of the shop rates; the merchant's buyer is 'village'.

goods:     per-merchant overrides for single goods: target, stock0 (starting stock), mult (regional price multiplier: below 1 cheap here, above 1 dear), flow (units a day made or eaten), fixed (one-of-a-kind), buyPct.

kindDepth is the standard target stock by kind of good; priceTiers scales it by how cheap the good is (cheap goods are held deep, costly ones shallow). One-of-a-kind goods are the ones the shop rules already sell once only (not stackable, not a counted salvage or ingredient): they are fixed and never move, except the ids listed under 'ordinary' (the plain rings, which the user ruled ordinary goods on 2026-10-24).

appetite._readme: A commodity market spends at most this share of its purse (its target) on ONE good a day (2026-10-24, the user: a hill village would not throw all its gold at wool or timber it has lived without). stocked: a good the market holds; unstocked: a good with no maker in its reach.

rumor._readme: Rumors (web/mygame/tradebook.js, equipment.txt market_rumor_check): once a day at each open market, in the open hours, the player quietly rolls the best of Perception, Investigation and Persuasion against the DC of the market's tier. A success teaches them the prices of the nearest market they hold no data for (the next nearest when they hold it, and when they hold every one, it freshens the oldest). dc: by the market's tier. memory: how many markets the trade book holds, visited and heard each (the hover card shows exactly these). age: [margin, days old] pairs, the first whose margin is met applies (beat the DC by 5 or more: today's prices; by 1 to 4: two days old; just meeting it: three). A natural 20 teaches two markets. swing: how far a good's price level must have moved (as a fraction) over the last 30 days for a rumor to mention it (news is change; a lasting gap, like fish far from the sea, is not).

settlements._readme: Who lives where (2026-10-24, proposed by Claude from each settlement's size on the map; the user may change them; anon is how a rumor or a board may refer to the place, never its name): the people a settlement feeds, by overworld tile. A settlement that makes nothing still eats; a tile without a market (Whitefold) still draws on the makers and still counts.

bw.name: Brinewick
bw.anon: a salt village on the tidal flats

world._readme: The food-cycle model (web/mygame/world.js, tools/gen_world.js). margin: the region's makers can turn out this many times what every settlement eats; coverFloor: a maker can always turn out at least this many times what the settlements drawing on it want of it, so no settlement is starved for ever just because its only maker in reach is a small one; pullExp: a settlement's pull on a maker is (population / 1000) ^ this, so a big city outbids a village when there is not enough to go round; capExp: a maker's capacity share is its tier weight x population ^ this; minDemand: units a day every settlement wants of every good at least (so every market feels its own makers).

demand._readme: Units a day that a thousand people use of each commodity (a unit is one item: a sack, a loaf, a bar). A good that is only worked (iron ore, hides) has none here and is eaten by industry below.

industry._readme: What a settlement's trades eat, units a day: forges eat ore and charcoal, weavers wool, tanneries hides, smiths bars.

dseason._readme: How demand swings over the year (spring, summer, autumn, winter; a year averages 1): fuel and wool and furs in winter, salt for the autumn curing, sausage in the cold. Anything not listed is flat.

inputs._readme: What a ware is worked from, for the shops that carry a tile and "inputs": true (a smith, a tailor, a general store): the share of its price that is the cost of each input commodity. A ware's price level follows (1 - the shares) + each share x the input's price ratio at the shop's tile (web/mygame/world.js), so iron bars and leather and cloth going up or down move the smiths' and tailors' prices. byItem beats byKind. Jewelry, one-of-a-kind pieces, potions, scrolls and food are not listed.

events._readme: Long named events (2026-10-24, the user: 30 to 90 days, about one at each settlement every year or two, a blight lowers the next year a little). web/mygame/world.js schedules them from the world seed: each settlement (tile) gets a string of events, one after another, each with a kind picked by weight from the kinds listed for the tile, a length in days, and magnitudes inside the ranges below; the regional kinds (tile "*") hit the whole region. An event ramps in over envelope.rise days, holds, and ramps out over envelope.fall days; a kind with an aftermath leaves the output lowered by frac of the dip, fading over its days. spacing: days between the END of one event and the START of the next at one tile; season: [first, last] day of the year the event may START (0 = the first of Aries; spring 0-89, summer 90-179, autumn 180-269, winter 270-359). effects: output (what the makers of the goods at the tile turn out), export (what the tile's makers send OUT to other settlements; the tile keeps what it eats), demand (what the settlement wants). mag is the multiplier at the peak. cause is for the rumors and notice boards.

commodity._readme: The distance model for open markets (see tools/gen_markets.js). perMile: the price rises this share of the base for every mile from the nearest maker; capLevel: the dearest it gets; cost: the price level AT the source (a major maker sells under the base, a minor one at it); supplyHalf: the miles at which a maker's share of a market's shelf has halved (it keeps falling, never to nothing); weight: a maker's share of a usual shelf; minSupply: below this a market makes nothing of a good; unsuppliedShare and useRate: a market with no supply wants a thin shelf (a share of the usual) and uses a share of it each day.
